title: Physiological and psychological responses to tended plant communities with varying color characteristics

findings.antecedent: Physiological data (alpha wave activity, 8-13 Hz)
findings.mechanism: Alpha waves are related to mental relaxation and calmness, which aligns with subjective reports of relaxation.

findings.antecedent: Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing plant images (all stimuli)
findings.mechanism: Women exhibited higher alpha wave power, indicating they were more relaxed than men.

findings.antecedent: Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing plant images (all stimuli)
findings.mechanism: Women reported higher subjective ratings, indicating they were more relaxed than men.

findings.antecedent: Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing one-color plant images
findings.mechanism: Women produced higher alpha wave power, indicating greater relaxation.

findings.antecedent: Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing one-color plant images
Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing two-color plant images
findings.mechanism: Women produced higher alpha wave power, indicating greater relaxation.

findings.antecedent: Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing two-color plant images
Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing three-color plant images
findings.mechanism: Women produced higher alpha wave power, indicating greater relaxation.

findings.antecedent: Female gender (vs. Male gender) viewing three-color plant images
findings.mechanism: Significant gender differences emerged when viewing tricolored plant compositions.

findings.antecedent: Plant communities containing two colors (vs. one or three colors)
findings.mechanism: The number of colors in plant communities affected the relaxation effect, with two colors being optimal.
findings.quote: the scores for the plant communities containing two colors (3.28±0.06) were highest, and were significantly different to those for plant communities containing one (2.75±0.14) and three colors (2.97±0.05) (F=7.02, p<0.01).

findings.antecedent: Number of colors in plant communities (one, two, or three)
findings.mechanism: No significant difference was found in alpha wave power across different numbers of colors when analyzed as a whole.
findings.quote: Overall, there was no significant difference between the three types of images.

findings.antecedent: Green plant communities (100% green, G100)
findings.mechanism: Green plants are associated with calm and comfort, leading to higher relaxation scores.
findings.quote: the relaxation experience scores were highest for green plant communities (3.58±0.16), and lowest for red plant communities (1.89±0.19).

findings.antecedent: Red plant communities (100% red, R100)
findings.mechanism: Red color is associated with arousal and negative emotions, reducing relaxation.
findings.quote: the relaxation experience scores were highest for green plant communities (3.58±0.16), and lowest for red plant communities (1.89±0.19).

findings.antecedent: Green plant communities (100% green, G100)
findings.mechanism: Green plants induce stronger relaxation effects.
findings.quote: The strongest a wave activity occurred when viewing the green stimulus image G100 (34.65±0.12)

findings.antecedent: Red plant communities (100% red, R100)
findings.mechanism: Red plants induce weaker relaxation effects.
findings.quote: the weakest occurred when viewing the red stimulation image R100 (34.20±0.12).

findings.antecedent: Green plant communities (100% green, G100) vs. Yellow plant communities (100% yellow, Y100)
findings.mechanism: Both green and yellow plant communities exert similar relaxation effects.
findings.quote: There were no significant differences in a wave activity between images containing green and yellow Y100 (34.57±0.13).

findings.antecedent: Green + yellow plant communities (G55Y45)
findings.mechanism: Green and yellow combinations are associated with joy and relaxation.
findings.quote: the plant community score was highest for G55Y45 (3.71±0.12)

findings.antecedent: Yellow + red plant communities (Y55R45 or R55Y45)
findings.mechanism: Yellow and red combinations are associated with less relaxation.
findings.quote: whereas the subjective scores of Y55R45 (2.86±0.16) and R55Y45 (2.90±0.12) were significantly lower (p<0.05).

findings.antecedent: Green + yellow plant communities (G55Y45)
findings.mechanism: Green + yellow combination exerted stronger relaxation effects.
findings.quote: The strongest a wave activity was elicited by green-yellow G55Y45 (34.83 ±0.14) images

findings.antecedent: Red + yellow plant communities (R55Y45)
findings.mechanism: Red + yellow combination exerted weaker relaxation effects.
findings.quote: The weakest a wave activity was elicited by red-yellow R55Y45 (33.83 ±0.13) images

findings.antecedent: Plant community with 55% green + 20% red + 25% yellow (G55R20Y25)
findings.mechanism: Optimal color proportion and balanced distribution of colors enhance relaxation.
findings.quote: G55R20Y25 (3.64±0.15) had the highest subjective score

findings.antecedent: Plant community with 55% yellow + 10% green + 35% red (Y55G10R35) or 55% red + 35% yellow + 10% green (R55Y35G10)
findings.mechanism: High proportion of yellow + red is associated with irritability and nervousness.
findings.quote: The scores of R55Y35G10 and Y55G10R35 were the lowest.

findings.antecedent: Plant community with 55% green + 20% red + 25% yellow (G55R20Y25)
findings.mechanism: Optimal color proportion and balanced distribution of colors enhance relaxation.
findings.quote: The strongest a wave activity was observed for G55R20Y25 (34.96±0.13)

findings.antecedent: Plant community with 55% red + 30% yellow + 15% green (R55Y30G15)
findings.mechanism: High proportion of yellow + red leads to weaker relaxation effects.
findings.quote: The weakest a wave activity was observed for R55Y30G15 (33.03 ±0.12), which was not significantly different (p>0.05) from R55Y35G10 (33.14±0.12), Y55G15R30 (33.36±0.12), and Y55G10R35 (33.25 ±0.12) images.

findings.antecedent: Plant communities with two or three different colors (vs. one solid color)
findings.mechanism: Color diversity in plant communities enhances restorative experiences.
findings.quote: those of foliage with combinations of two or three colors induced stronger responses than images with a single color.

stimuli.description: Images of tended plant communities in Shenyang, China, with varying combinations of green, yellow, and red foliage. Stimuli were manipulated for color type (one, two, or three colors), color ratio (e.g., 100% single color, 55%+45% two colors, 55%+x%+(45-x)% three colors), and color position (lower hedge fixed, upper bushes varied). The base image was a deciduous tree + evergreen tree + shrub + lawn multi-layer plant community.

limitations: Subjects were undergraduates and postgraduates aged between 18 and 27, limiting generalizability to the broader public.
The sample size was relatively small (40 participants).
Stimuli depicted visual scenes from one particular climate, resulting in relatively monotonous plant color types.
Photoshop software was used for image processing and color recognition, which may be less accurate than MATLAB or Python.
Additional research is needed to fully explore the effects of color proportion and position gradient.
Future research should investigate the effects of plant color on non-human animals, given their different visual perception abilities and needs.
